fields.name: Entities
fields.evidence: 48 bytes = HashSet (bg3.exe creator bg3.exe+0x2B99A60, 426 bytes like the other HashSet singletons, no element destructor). esv::death::DeathSystem::Update (EoCServer.dll+0xCB30A0) ends by moving the frame's dead-entity set into the singleton with the generic 8-byte-key HashSet move EoCServer.dll+0x28E750 (the same helper family used for HashSet<EntityHandle> elsewhere). Readers: `anonymous`::FindPlayerEntity (macOS index), esv::death::CombatEntityAssignmentSystem query (bg3.exe+0x2345A70). Live (seen.py, idle): one instance, all bytes zero (empty container). Windows: creator bg3.exe+0x2B99A60 registers 0x30-byte storage with the plain-key HashSet destructor and zeroes the set; the DeathSystem update bg3.exe+0x2B8DEC0 ends by move-assigning (bg3.exe+0x5DF700) its frame-data set at FrameData+0x180 into this singleton (query DAT_14638356C, registered by bg3.exe+0x2B9B340). That frame-data set has 8-byte keys: bg3.exe+0x2B927E0 looks up query entities in it (buckets +0x180, count +0x188, next ids +0x190, keys +0x1A0 compared as 8-byte entity handles).

open_questions: What exactly qualifies an entity for the set (dead this frame vs. dead and not yet resurrected) is not traced.
second_pass: Confirmed on Windows: DeathSystem update bg3.exe+0x2B8DEC0 moves its FrameData+0x180 set into the singleton, and bg3.exe+0x2B927E0 shows that set's keys are 8-byte entity handles of its query.
